key_insight: Trigonal selenium appears intrinsically defect tolerant because defect-mediated recombination is strongly suppressed, even when deep gap states are present.
engineering_relevance: This suggests t-Se is a promising wide-band-gap absorber for tandem and indoor photovoltaics, where defect tolerance can help preserve device efficiency.
method: First-principles calculations of a large and chemically diverse set of point defects in trigonal selenium
Evaluation of defect-assisted Shockley-Read-Hall recombination pathways, including radiative and nonradiative multi-phonon capture
Analysis of how defect level position, lattice relaxation, charge state, and doping conditions affect recombination rates
evidence_signal: The study reports that realistic point-defect concentrations in t-Se cannot explain the observed efficiency losses because both nonradiative and radiative defect-assisted recombination remain too small.
watch_item: The conclusion is based on computed defect physics, so device performance may still depend on uncontrolled extrinsic defects, interfaces, or processing-induced disorder not captured here.
paper_title: Defect Tolerance in Trigonal Selenium Photovoltaics
